summary.text: 六 is the numeral “six,” already attested in oracle-bone records as a cardinal number and in a month name. Its graphic origin is disputed: proposed explanations include a shelter picture, a conventional counting mark, or a graph once similar to 入.

formation.text: The formation remains disputed, and no component breakdown is established. The shelter-picture proposal would make the whole graph pictographic; other proposals treat it as a conventional counting mark or as a graph later distinguished from 入. The Shuowen analysis of 入 and 八 through 易 numerology is a historical interpretation that the paleographic discussion considers unlikely to preserve the original graphic meaning.

history.text: The selected oracle-script-style and Western Zhou bronze-script-style images are modern digital reconstructions. Their different forms illustrate the labeled script styles but do not establish a sequence of graphic changes or settle the origin.
The Shuowen explanation connects 六 with 入 and 八 through 易 numerology; this is a historical account, not a demonstrated graphic breakdown.

uncertainties.text: The origin proposals remain unresolved: a shelter associated with 廬, differentiation from 入, or a conventional counting mark. The cited numeral uses do not decide among them.
The proposed borrowing from a shelter word is unconfirmed: the shelter’s name and pronunciation are not independently established, and the cited Old Chinese reconstructions for 六 and 廬 differ.

senses.text: Cited oracle-bone records use 六 as a cardinal numeral in “six sheep” and in a month name meaning “sixth month.” They attest both uses but do not establish which came first.

limitations.text: The earliest cited evidence already uses 六 as a numeral. A prior shelter meaning and a transition from that meaning to “six” are not established; the proposed sound-based borrowing remains unconfirmed.
The relative chronology of the cardinal and ordinal uses is unresolved.

overview.text: 六 means “six.” Oracle-bone records already use it as a numeral, while its original graphic explanation remains disputed.

takeaway.text: The idea that a shelter picture was reused for “six” because its name sounded similar is only a proposal; the shelter’s name and sound match are unconfirmed.
